title: Kit of Parts
description: The slot directory for one style. Version 0.2.0 is a direct response to authoring the Georgian kit end to end, which found four structural flaws in 0.1.0: prohibitions could only be written as prose, parameters had no types or units or provenance, a child could only replace a whole slot when it wanted to change one field, and nothing recorded a conflict between a period dimension and a code requirement. All four are now data.

binding.description: specified: this style fixes the slot and stops the cascade. extends: MERGE into the inherited value rather than replacing it — parameters merge by key, variants apply their add/remove/reorder. This is the fix for the commonest authoring case, where a child wants to change one number in a slot whose other fields remain true. open: unspecified, cascades. forbidden: prohibited outright, stops the cascade.

variants.description: Records, not bare strings. Most of what a style says about a slot is which options it REFUSES, and in 0.1.0 those refusals could only be written as prose no engine would read. The Georgian kit had two slot-level prohibitions and about twenty-five variant-level ones.

status.description: canonical: the default a generator should reach for. permitted: correct but not first choice. atypical: defensible only with a reason. forbidden: wrong, and the note should say why.

op.description: Only on an `extends` binding: how this record acts on the inherited list.

parameters.description: A map of TYPED records. In 0.1.0 this was free-form, and a range, an enumerated set and a ratio were all indistinguishable arrays of numbers with their units surviving only in the key name.

rule.description: One sentence stating the constraint that governs the slot.

determined_by.description: Slot ids that decide this slot, where it is not an independent variable. A portico soffit is whatever the bound order's entablature requires; specifying it separately either restates the order or contradicts it.

code_conflict.description: Where the period dimension and the building code disagree. First-class data for a kit that is meant to be buildable, and in 0.1.0 it had to be repeated as prose in three separate balustrade slots.

packs.description: Proportion packs that speak to this slot, in precedence order, nearest first. PRECEDENCE OF PRECEDENCES: a slot-level packs block outranks the style node's proportion_packs.precedence, which outranks pack order of binding. Where two rulings survive at equal rank the resolver must report the disagreement rather than choose.

in_calibration.description: False where the bound context falls outside the rule's calibrated range. A rule outside calibration still evaluates and should not be trusted.

calibrated_range.description: Added in 0.2.1. `in_calibration` is a boolean authored at one context, and calibration is a range: whether trim-classical governs the chair rail depends on the ceiling, with the crossover at 142.5 in. Evaluable like everything else.

binding.description: which bound variable the range applies to, e.g. ceiling_height

judgment.description: The sources do not determine this and a designer must decide. Marking it honestly is worth more than a number nobody can defend.

invented.description: Authored rather than retrieved — there is no historical precedent at all. The garage is the standing example: no traditional style has an answer, because none had to.

assets.description: asset ids illustrating this slot, correct and incorrect

rule_append.description: Only on an `extends` binding: a clause appended to the inherited rule sentence. Added in 0.2.1 — `extends` fixed three of four restatement cases and failed on the fourth because `rule` is one string with no merge operator, so a child adding a clause had to restate the whole sentence or leave the resolved rule silent about its own change.

edit_provenance.description: Added in 0.2.1. `judgment` and `invented` describe the slot; on an `extends` binding they are inherited and say nothing about whether the CHILD's delta is itself invention or retrieval.

applies_when.description: Conditionality. A style spanning a century does not have one value per slot: the Georgian sash runs 12/12 to 9/6 to 6/6, the fanlight does not exist before about 1780, and butt hinges arrive around 1775. In 0.1.0 these had to be buried in nested objects no engine could act on.

parameter.description: Exactly one of value, range, set or expr.

expr.description: Evaluable by the proportion engine in the bound context.

computed_at.description: The value the expression yields in a stated reference context, so the file is readable by a person and not only by an engine.

unit.description: Required on anything dimensional. Units surviving only in key names was the single most fragile thing about 0.1.0.

kind.description: measured: from surviving fabric or a documented standard. derived: computed from a proportion pack. editorial: our considered convention. invented: no precedent exists. code: imposed from outside. A brick course, a stair riser band and a garage setback were indistinguishable in 0.1.0 and are three completely different kinds of claim.

diagnostic.description: This parameter is designed to fail informatively rather than to prescribe.

pack.description: Which proportion pack the expression evaluates against. Required whenever `expr` is present — an expression with no pack cannot be checked or recomputed.
